description: Control objects and view containers beyond the basic Slider/Button/Checkbox set: 2D and interval sliders, setters and togglers, locators, click and gesture panes, animators, tabbed/opener/flip views, and the options and helper functions that make Dynamic interfaces responsive.

tools.name: Slider2D
tools.description: A two-dimensional slider whose value is a point {x, y} in a rectangle; the Manipulate equivalent is {{p, {0.5, 0.5}}, {0, 0}, {1, 1}}. Use it to control two coupled parameters such as a position or a complex number.
tools.usage:
Slider2D[Dynamic[pt]]
Slider2D[Dynamic[pt], {{xmin, ymin}, {xmax, ymax}}]
Slider2D[Dynamic[pt], {{xmin, ymin}, {xmax, ymax}, {dx, dy}}]

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: Corner points and optional step sizes.

tools.name: IntervalSlider
tools.description: A slider with two thumbs whose value is an interval {min, max}. Use it to select ranges (e.g. time windows or thresholds) in data-exploration interfaces; options control minimum interval size and thumb behaviour.
tools.usage:
IntervalSlider[Dynamic[{a, b}]]
IntervalSlider[Dynamic[{a, b}], {min, max}]
IntervalSlider[Dynamic[{a, b}], {min, max, step}]

tools.name: VerticalSlider
tools.description: A vertically oriented slider with the same value semantics as Slider. Use it for level-style controls (volume, height) and compact side panels.
tools.usage:
VerticalSlider[Dynamic[x]]
VerticalSlider[Dynamic[x], {min, max, step}]

tools.name: ColorSlider
tools.description: A slider that lets the user pick a colour (hue strip with lightness/saturation control); ColorSetter is the swatch-button alternative that opens the system colour dialog. Both work with Dynamic colour variables and in Manipulate via {c, Red} specifications.
tools.usage:
ColorSlider[Dynamic[c]]
ColorSetter[Dynamic[c]]

parameters.name: c
parameters.description: Dynamic variable holding an RGBColor/Hue value.

tools.example:
DynamicModule[{c = Red}, Row[{ColorSlider[Dynamic[c]], Dynamic[Graphics[{c, Disk[]}, ImageSize -> 60]]}]]
Manipulate[Plot[Sin[x], {x, 0, 6}, PlotStyle -> c], {c, Blue}]

tools.name: Setter
tools.description: Setter[Dynamic[x], val] is a button that sets x to val and appears pressed while x equals val; SetterBar[Dynamic[x], {val1, val2, ...}] builds a row of mutually exclusive setters (the toolbar-style radio control used by Manipulate for small discrete choices).
tools.usage:
Setter[Dynamic[x], val]
Setter[Dynamic[x], val, label]
SetterBar[Dynamic[x], {val1, val2, ...}]
SetterBar[Dynamic[x], {val1 -> lbl1, ...}]
tools.example: DynamicModule[{f = Sin}, Column[{SetterBar[Dynamic[f], {Sin, Cos, Tan}], Dynamic[Plot[f[x], {x, 0, 2 Pi}]]}]]

tools.name: Toggler
tools.description: Toggler[Dynamic[x], {val1, val2, ...}] cycles x through a list of values each time it is clicked, displaying the current value (or a custom display per value); TogglerBar shows a row of toggle buttons whose pressed set is a list. Use them for boolean-like or multi-select settings.
tools.usage:
Toggler[Dynamic[x]]
Toggler[Dynamic[x], {val1 -> disp1, val2 -> disp2, ...}]
TogglerBar[Dynamic[list], {val1, val2, ...}]

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: For TogglerBar: dynamic list of currently selected values.

tools.example: DynamicModule[{on = {"grid"}}, Column[{TogglerBar[Dynamic[on], {"grid", "frame", "legend"}], Dynamic[Plot[Sin[x], {x, 0, 6}, GridLines -> If[MemberQ[on, "grid"], Automatic, None], Frame -> MemberQ[on, "frame"]]]}]]

tools.name: RadioButton
tools.description: RadioButton[Dynamic[x], val] is a single radio button selected when x === val; CheckboxBar[Dynamic[list], {vals}] is a row of labelled checkboxes whose selected values form a list. Together with RadioButtonBar they cover exclusive and multiple choice inputs.
tools.usage:
RadioButton[Dynamic[x], val]
CheckboxBar[Dynamic[list], {val1, val2, ...}]
CheckboxBar[Dynamic[list], {val1 -> lbl1, ...}]

parameters.name: x / list
parameters.description: Dynamic variable holding the selected value(s).

tools.name: ButtonBar
tools.description: ButtonBar[{lbl1 :> act1, lbl2 :> act2, ...}] lays out several buttons in a row with consistent styling; ActionMenu[label, {lbl :> act, ...}] gives a drop-down menu of actions instead. Use them for command toolbars in custom interfaces.
tools.usage:
ButtonBar[{lbl1 :> act1, lbl2 :> act2, ...}]
ActionMenu[label, {lbl1 :> act1, lbl2 :> act2, ...}]
tools.example:
ButtonBar[{"Run" :> run[], "Reset" :> (x = 0), "Export" :> Export["out.png", plot]}]
ActionMenu["File", {"Open" :> open[], "Save" :> save[]}]

tools.name: DefaultButton
tools.description: DefaultButton[action] and CancelButton[action] are the standard OK/Cancel buttons for dialogs: they take the platform's default/cancel appearance and respond to Enter / Escape. Typically used inside DialogInput with DialogReturn.
tools.usage:
DefaultButton[]
DefaultButton[action]
DefaultButton[label, action]
CancelButton[]
CancelButton[action]

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Expression evaluated on click (defaults to DialogReturn[] / DialogReturn[$Canceled]).

tools.name: FileNameSetter
tools.description: A button that opens the system file dialog and stores the chosen file name in a Dynamic variable ("Open", "Save" or "Directory" modes). Use it for file-picking in Manipulate-style interfaces without writing dialog code.
tools.usage:
FileNameSetter[Dynamic[name]]
FileNameSetter[Dynamic[name], "Save"]
FileNameSetter[Dynamic[name], "Open", {"CSV" -> {"*.csv"}}]
tools.example: DynamicModule[{f = None}, Column[{FileNameSetter[Dynamic[f]], Dynamic[If[StringQ[f], Import[f], "no file"]]}]]

tools.name: ListPicker
tools.description: A scrollable list box in which the user selects one or more items; the selected values are stored in a Dynamic list. Use it for choosing from long lists (columns, files, entities) where a PopupMenu would be unwieldy.
tools.usage:
ListPicker[Dynamic[sel], {val1, val2, ...}]
ListPicker[Dynamic[sel], {val1 -> lbl1, ...}, Multiselection -> False]

tools.name: Locator
tools.description: A draggable point in a graphic whose position is a Dynamic variable; used inside Graphics (or via LocatorPane) to let users move control points, sources or vertices interactively. In Manipulate, {{p, {0, 0}}, Locator} declares a locator control.
tools.usage:
Graphics[{Locator[Dynamic[p]]}]
Locator[Dynamic[p], appearance]
Manipulate[expr, {{p, {0, 0}}, Locator}]

parameters.name: appearance
parameters.description: Graphics used to draw the locator (Automatic, None, or custom).

tools.name: LocatorPane
tools.description: LocatorPane[Dynamic[pts], graphics] overlays one or more draggable locators on a graphic and keeps their coordinates in a Dynamic variable; LocatorAutoCreate -> True lets users add/remove locators with Alt-click. The standard tool for interactive curve editing, control polygons and point-set demos.
tools.usage:
LocatorPane[Dynamic[pt], graphics]
LocatorPane[Dynamic[{pt1, pt2, ...}], graphics]
LocatorPane[Dynamic[pts], graphics, {{xmin, ymin}, {xmax, ymax}}, LocatorAutoCreate -> True]

parameters.name: pts
parameters.description: Dynamic point or list of points.

tools.example:
DynamicModule[{pts = {{0, 0}, {1, 2}, {3, 1}, {4, 3}}},
 LocatorPane[Dynamic[pts], Dynamic[Graphics[{BezierCurve[pts], Dashed, Line[pts]}, PlotRange -> {{-1, 5}, {-1, 4}}, Frame -> True]], LocatorAutoCreate -> True]]

tools.name: ClickPane
tools.description: ClickPane[graphics, f] calls f with the clicked coordinate (in the graphics coordinate system) whenever the user clicks inside the pane. Use it for point placement, region selection and simple drawing tools; EventHandler gives finer control over mouse events.
tools.usage:
ClickPane[graphics, f]
ClickPane[Dynamic[graphics], f]
tools.example: DynamicModule[{pts = {}}, ClickPane[Dynamic[Graphics[{PointSize[Large], Point[pts]}, PlotRange -> 1, Frame -> True]], AppendTo[pts, #] &]]

tools.name: Trigger
tools.description: A control with play/pause/stop buttons that advances a variable over a range at a given rate, without Animator's slider; in Manipulate, {t, 0, 10, Trigger} or the default for time-like variables. Use it to drive simulations and animations under user control.
tools.usage:
Trigger[Dynamic[t], {min, max}]
Trigger[Dynamic[t], {min, max, dt}]
Manipulate[expr, {t, 0, 10, Trigger}]

tools.name: Animator
tools.description: Animator[Dynamic[t], {min, max}] is the animation control used by Animate: a slider with play controls that continuously updates t. Options AnimationRate, AnimationDirection, AnimationRepetitions and AppearanceElements customize speed, direction and visible buttons. Use it directly when building animations inside DynamicModule.
tools.usage:
Animator[Dynamic[t]]
Animator[Dynamic[t], {min, max}]
Animator[Dynamic[t], {min, max, step}, AnimationRate -> r]
tools.example: DynamicModule[{t = 0}, Column[{Animator[Dynamic[t], {0, 2 Pi}, AnimationRate -> 1], Dynamic[Graphics[{Disk[{Cos[t], Sin[t]}, 0.1]}, PlotRange -> 1.2]]}]]

tools.name: Manipulator
tools.description: The composite slider-plus-animation control that Manipulate uses by default for numeric variables: a slider with an expandable panel offering play, step and input field. Use it standalone in DynamicModule interfaces to get Manipulate-style controls.
tools.usage:
Manipulator[Dynamic[x]]
Manipulator[Dynamic[x], {min, max}]
Manipulator[Dynamic[x], {min, max, step}]

parameters.name: Appearance
parameters.description: Option: "Open" shows the extra controls expanded.

tools.name: TabView
tools.description: Displays several expressions in a tabbed panel; the visible tab can be bound to a Dynamic variable. Use it to organise multi-page interfaces and reports (e.g. plot / data / settings tabs).
tools.usage:
TabView[{expr1, expr2, ...}]
TabView[{lbl1 -> expr1, lbl2 -> expr2, ...}]
TabView[{lbl -> expr, ...}, Dynamic[i]]
TabView[..., ControlPlacement -> Left]

parameters.name: i
parameters.description: Dynamic index or label of the visible tab.

tools.name: OpenerView
tools.description: OpenerView[{header, body}] shows a disclosure triangle with header that expands to reveal body; Opener is the bare triangle control. Use it for collapsible sections, nested tree displays and optional details.
tools.usage:
OpenerView[{header, body}]
OpenerView[{header, body}, True]
OpenerView[{header, body}, Dynamic[open]]
Opener[Dynamic[open]]
tools.example:
OpenerView[{"Advanced options", Column[{Checkbox[Dynamic[a]], Slider[Dynamic[b]]}]}]
Column[OpenerView[{#["name"], #["details"]}] & /@ records]

tools.name: MenuView
tools.description: Shows one of several expressions selected through a popup menu, the drop-down analogue of TabView; SlideView shows them as a slide show with previous/next buttons, FlipView flips through them on click, and PaneSelector picks a pane by an arbitrary Dynamic key.
tools.usage:
MenuView[{lbl1 -> expr1, lbl2 -> expr2, ...}]
SlideView[{expr1, expr2, ...}]
FlipView[{expr1, expr2, ...}]
PaneSelector[{key1 -> expr1, key2 -> expr2, ...}, Dynamic[key]]

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: For PaneSelector: Dynamic value selecting the pane.

tools.example:
MenuView[Table[ToString[f] -> Plot[f[x], {x, 0, 10}], {f, {Sin, Cos, Tan}}]]
SlideView[Table[Plot[Sin[k x], {x, 0, 2 Pi}], {k, 5}]]
PaneSelector[{True -> "running", False -> "idle"}, Dynamic[busy]]

tools.name: TableView
tools.description: Displays a matrix or list of rows as an editable, scrollable spreadsheet-like grid with row/column headers; changes can be bound to a Dynamic variable. Use it for viewing and editing tabular data interactively inside a notebook.
tools.usage:
TableView[matrix]
TableView[Dynamic[matrix]]
TableView[{{...}}, ItemSize -> 8]

parameters.name: matrix
parameters.description: List of rows (or Dynamic for editing).

tools.notes: Introduced in 12.1. For read-only display prefer Dataset or Grid.

tools.name: ControlActive
tools.description: ControlActive[act, norm] evaluates to act while a control (slider, locator) is being dragged and to norm otherwise. Use it to render a cheap preview during interaction and the full-quality version when the user releases - the key technique for responsive Manipulate interfaces.
tools.usage: ControlActive[act, norm]

parameters.name: act
parameters.description: Value while the control is active (e.g. low PlotPoints).

tools.example: Manipulate[Plot3D[Sin[a x y], {x, 0, 3}, {y, 0, 3}, PlotPoints -> ControlActive[10, 40], MaxRecursion -> ControlActive[0, 2]], {a, 1, 5}]
tools.notes: ContinuousAction -> False on the control is the coarser alternative (update only on release).

tools.name: MousePosition
tools.description: Gives the current mouse position in the specified coordinate system ("Graphics", "GraphicsScaled", "CellContents", "WindowAbsolute", "ScreenAbsolute"); normally used inside Dynamic to make hover-following displays. MouseAnnotation gives the annotation of the object under the mouse.
tools.usage:
Dynamic[MousePosition[]]
Dynamic[MousePosition["Graphics"]]
MousePosition["Graphics", None]

parameters.name: default
parameters.description: Value when the mouse is outside (default None).

tools.name: GestureHandler
tools.description: Attaches touch-gesture actions ("Tap", "Drag", "Pinch", "Rotate", "Swipe") to an expression on touch-capable devices, the touch analogue of EventHandler. Use it in interfaces deployed to Wolfram Player on tablets.
tools.usage: GestureHandler[expr, {"gesture1" :> act1, "gesture2" :> act2, ...}]

parameters.name: gesture :> act
parameters.description: Gesture name and action; TouchPosition[] and GestureSetting give details inside act.

tools.name: Enabled
tools.description: Option for all controls (Button, Slider, InputField, ...) that greys out and disables the control when False; combine with Dynamic to enable controls conditionally. Appearance customises the look (e.g. "Palette", "Frameless", "Labeled", or image-based) and ImageSize the dimensions.
tools.usage:
Button["Run", run[], Enabled -> Dynamic[ready]]
Slider[Dynamic[x], Appearance -> "Labeled"]
Button["x", act, Appearance -> "Palette"]
tools.example: DynamicModule[{ok = False}, Column[{Checkbox[Dynamic[ok]], Button["Proceed", Print["go"], Enabled -> Dynamic[ok]]}]]

tools.name: Setting
tools.description: Setting[expr] replaces every Dynamic and control in expr by its current value, turning an interactive expression into a static one; DynamicSetting[expr] is the inverse marker that makes a control return its value when used as input. Use Setting to snapshot the state of an interface (e.g. inside a Button action).
tools.usage:
Setting[expr]
DynamicSetting[control]

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Expression containing Dynamic or control objects.

tools.example:
Setting[Slider[Dynamic[x]]] (* current value of x *)
Button["Snapshot", snap = Setting[Dynamic[plot]]]

tools.name: ControllerState
tools.description: Reads the state of external controllers (gamepads, joysticks, 3D mice) as Dynamic-updatable values, and ControllerInformation lists connected devices. Manipulate can bind variables to controller axes via ControllerLinking. Use it for hardware-driven interactive demonstrations.
tools.usage:
ControllerState["prop"]
ControllerState[dev, "prop"]
ControllerInformation[]
Manipulate[..., ControllerLinking -> True]

tools.name: AttachCell
tools.description: Attaches a floating cell (tooltip-like popup, palette fragment or annotation) to a notebook, cell or box at a given position; returns a CellObject that can be removed with NotebookDelete. Used to implement custom code assistants, inline previews and context menus.
tools.usage:
AttachCell[obj, cellexpr]
AttachCell[obj, cellexpr, {pos, offset}]
AttachCell[obj, cellexpr, {Left, Top}, {Left, Bottom}, "ClosingActions" -> {"OutsideMouseClick"}]

parameters.name: obj
parameters.description: NotebookObject, CellObject or BoxObject to attach to.

parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: Anchor position on the target and on the attached cell.

tools.example:
cell = AttachCell[EvaluationCell[], Cell[BoxData[ToBoxes[Style["note", Red]]], "Text"], {Right, Top}, 0, {Left, Top}];
NotebookDelete[cell]

tools.name: Deployed
tools.description: Option (and Deploy wrapper) that when True makes an interface non-editable for the user while keeping controls functional - the state used for CDF/Player deployment and FormFunction previews. SaveDefinitions -> True in Manipulate embeds required definitions, and Initialization runs setup code when the interface is first displayed.
tools.usage:
Manipulate[expr, controls, SaveDefinitions -> True]
Manipulate[expr, controls, Initialization :> (Needs["pkg`"])]
DynamicModule[{x}, body, Deployed -> True]

parameters.name: SaveDefinitions
parameters.description: Manipulate option: store definitions of user functions with the output.

parameters.name: Initialization
parameters.description: Held code run when the DynamicModule/Manipulate is first evaluated.

tools.example:
f[x_] := x^2 Sin[x];
Manipulate[Plot[f[a x], {x, 0, 10}], {a, 1, 5}, SaveDefinitions -> True]

tools.name: DynamicWrapper
tools.description: DynamicWrapper[expr, dyn] displays expr but re-evaluates dyn (for side effects) whenever its dependencies change, without displaying dyn. Use it to run code such as logging or variable synchronisation in response to interface changes.
tools.usage:
DynamicWrapper[expr, dyn]
DynamicWrapper[expr, dyn, TrackedSymbols :> {x}]

tools.name: TrackedSymbols
tools.description: Option of Dynamic, DynamicModule, Manipulate and Refresh restricting which symbols trigger re-evaluation (TrackedSymbols :> {a, b}) - essential for performance when a Dynamic depends on many variables but should update for only some. Related timing options: UpdateInterval (periodic refresh) and SynchronousUpdating.
tools.usage:
Dynamic[expr, TrackedSymbols :> {x}]
Manipulate[expr, controls, TrackedSymbols :> {a}]
Dynamic[Now, UpdateInterval -> 1]

parameters.name: TrackedSymbols
parameters.description: Full (default), All, or a list of symbols.

parameters.name: SynchronousUpdating
parameters.description: True/False/Automatic: run updates on the front end thread.

tools.example:
DynamicModule[{a = 1, b = 2}, Column[{Slider[Dynamic[a]], Slider[Dynamic[b]], Dynamic[expensive[a], TrackedSymbols :> {a}]}]]
Dynamic[DateString[], UpdateInterval -> 1]

tools.name: FormControl
tools.description: FormControl[Dynamic[x], type] gives an input control appropriate for an Interpreter type (e.g. "Country", "Date", "Color", "Integer"), the same controls used by FormFunction pages, for use in local interfaces.
tools.usage:
FormControl[Dynamic[x], "type"]
FormControl[Dynamic[x], type, opts]

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Dynamic variable receiving the interpreted value.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Interpreter type or a control specification.

tools.name: AutoAction
tools.description: Option for Slider, Setter, Locator and similar controls that when True makes the control respond to the mouse hovering over it without clicking. Useful for scrubbing-style previews in demonstrations.
tools.usage: Slider[Dynamic[x], AutoAction -> True]

tools.name: ContinuousAction
tools.description: Option for Slider, InputField, Locator, Manipulate controls and others: True (default for sliders) updates the Dynamic value continuously while dragging, False only when the mouse is released or Enter is pressed. Set False for expensive computations that should not run at every pixel.
tools.usage:
Slider[Dynamic[x], ContinuousAction -> False]
Manipulate[expr, {x, 0, 1, ContinuousAction -> False}]

tools.name: MouseAppearance
tools.description: MouseAppearance[expr, cursor] changes the mouse cursor ("LinkHand", "Arrow", "DragAndDrop", a custom graphic...) while it is over expr; Mouseover (basic chunk) swaps the content instead. Use it to signal clickable regions in custom graphics.
tools.usage:
MouseAppearance[expr, "LinkHand"]
MouseAppearance[expr, Graphics[...]]
